questions.q: What technology do you use most often?
questions.answer: My laptop, without question. I use it all day at work for applications, emails and research, and in the evenings for studying. My phone is a close second, but the laptop is really the [[backbone]] of my working day.

questions.q: How does technology help you in your work?
questions.answer: Enormously. Almost every application is submitted online now, and I can hold video meetings with universities abroad. Tasks that once took days can be done in hours, which has [[streamlined]] our work considerably.

questions.q: Do you think you rely too much on technology?
questions.answer: To some extent, yes. It makes life easier, but I've noticed I reach for my phone out of habit rather than need. I'm trying to be more [[mindful]], especially in the evenings when I should be relaxing.

questions.q: Is there any piece of technology you'd like to buy?
questions.answer: I'd quite like a good e-reader. I read a lot, and carrying several books around isn't very practical. An e-reader would be lighter and easier on the eyes than my phone, so it seems a [[worthwhile]] investment.

questions.q: Do older people in your country find technology difficult?
questions.answer: Many do, although it's improving. My grandfather, for instance, now makes video calls to my elder sister, but it took a lot of patience to teach him. Once they see the benefits, older people can be surprisingly [[receptive]].
